classification.difficultyReason: Reverse the summary process to fix five positions in an ordered seven-value list, then choose two remaining entries within their ordering bounds to produce distinct valid sets.

content.prompt: Write down two sets of seven whole numbers with minimum data value 3, lower quartile 5, median 10, upper quartile 12 and maximum data value 13.

answer.worked:
For seven ordered values, the median is the fourth value. Excluding it, each half contains three values, so the lower and upper quartiles are the second and sixth values of the complete list.

The first, second, fourth, sixth and seventh values must therefore be $3,5,10,12,13$, respectively. Choose a third value between $5$ and $10$ and a fifth value between $10$ and $12$.

Two possible sets are:
$$3,5,7,10,12,12,13$$
$$3,5,6,10,11,12,13$$
Both have minimum $3$, lower quartile $5$, median $10$, upper quartile $12$ and maximum $13$.
